pages.title: Vacuum Stability
pages.text: $(thing)Vacuum Stability$()$(br2)What could stop a universe from starting at all? A vacuum energy a little larger and it would fly apart before stars formed; a Higgs coupling a little smaller and the vacuum would be unstable. Ours sits, by measurement, at the edge: metastable. Unlocks the Metastable Vacuum Lattice.

$(thing)Insight$(): 180$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Cosmic Inflation, The Standard Model.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Higgs Field Capacitor.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): The quartic coupling λ of the Higgs field is not a constant: it runs with the energy scale μ. The top quark, with Yukawa coupling y, dominates the running and drives λ down logarithmically from its value λ₀ at the top mass m. Write λ at scale μ in this top-dominated approximation.
